disposition_reason: JECFA 91 monograph prints GEMS/Food Cd occurrence for cocoa beans, butter, mass, powder, chocolate and cocoa beverage by cluster/WHO region (n, %<LOD, MB mean, median, P95), Cd in chocolate by cocoa-solids class and cocoa powder by producing cluster with Codex ML exceedance, plus extensive cocoa exposure-contribution analyses.

study.design: monitoring summary and dietary exposure assessment (JECFA monograph, WHO FAS 82)
study.material_scope: cocoa beans, cocoa butter, cocoa mass, cocoa powder, chocolate, cocoa beverage
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Records grouped by submitting country cluster (G03 Cameroon/Cote d'Ivoire/Ghana; G05 Brazil/Chile/Colombia/Ecuador/Peru; G09 Indonesia; G07 Australia; G08 Germany/Spain; G10 Canada/Japan/USA; WHO European Region). JECFA uses producer clusters as proxies for cocoa source; whether samples are domestic-grown cocoa or market products is not stated per record.
study.collection_period: records submitted to GEMS/Food since 1 January 2011 (sampling years not reported)
study.lod_loq: records with LOD above a 20 µg/kg cut-off excluded (Section 2.1); 46% of all records left-censored

77th JECFA (2013) recap: mean exposure from cocoa-containing foods 0.005-0.39 µg/kg bw/month (0.2-1.6% PTMI) across 17 cluster diets; individual cocoa products 0.001-0.46 (0.004-1.8% PTMI); highest P97.5 12 µg/kg bw/month for European children 7-11 y solely from cocoa powder; total diet incl. high cocoa 7.4-17.2 (adults) and 23.9 (children 0.5-12 y) µg/kg bw/month.

Germany (Fechner et al. 2019): cocoa consumption mean 0.028, P95 0.098 g/kg bw/day; cocoa-products Cd exposure 0.019 (median) and 0.131 (P95) µg/kg bw/week (0.081 and 0.56 µg/kg bw/month); cocoa ~1% of Cd exposure.

EFSA 2012 (as summarized by JECFA): cocoa products 0.2% (infants) to 9.4% (other children) of Cd exposure, mostly from chocolate; based on cocoa powder n=732, chocolate n=1558, cocoa beverages n=2196.

Australia (national nutrition survey, 24HDR): hot chocolate beverages, cocoa, chocolate and fudge contributed 4-6% of estimated Cd exposure; Western Australia study (Callan 2014) reported cocoa powder and chocolate among highest Cd foods but contributions not reported.
France TDS2: chocolate 1-2% of Cd exposure; French children 3-6 y (Glorennec 2016): chocolate 2%.

Other national: Cameroon 'sugar and cocoa products' 1%; Netherlands cocoa beans max 1%; New Zealand TDS cocoa 1% (adults) to 8% (children); Serbia chocolate 0.7%; Spain (Valencia) chocolate 1% of adult exposure despite second-highest mean Cd concentration.
